name: StructuredOutputNode Implementation & Repair Loop
query: Where is the StructuredOutputNode class defined in our repository, and what repair loop mechanism does it implement for malformed JSON?

retrieved_chunks.content:
class StructuredOutputNode:
    """
    Core reusable node enforcing Pydantic schema validation with an automated
    LLM repair loop to catch and fix malformed JSON responses.
    """
    def __init__(self, llm: Any, schema: Type[BaseModel], system_prompt: str, max_retries: int = 2):
        self.llm = llm
        self.schema = schema
        self.system_prompt = system_prompt
        self.max_retries = max_retries

    def invoke(self, user_prompt: str) -> BaseModel:
        attempts = 0
        messages = [SystemMessage(content=self.system_prompt), HumanMessage(content=user_prompt)]
        while attempts <= self.max_retries:
            raw_response = self.llm.invoke(messages)
            parsed, error_msg = self._validate(raw_response.content)
            if parsed is not None:
                return parsed
            attempts += 1
            messages.append(AIMessage(content=raw_response.content))
            messages.append(HumanMessage(content=f"Validation Error: {error_msg}. Return corrected valid JSON conforming to schema."))
        raise ValidationError(f"Failed to produce valid schema after {self.max_retries} retries.")

retrieval_context: StructuredOutputNode is defined in src/core/structured_output.py. It enforces Pydantic schema validation with an automated LLM repair loop (max_retries=2) that feeds back validation errors and asks the LLM to return corrected valid JSON.

Implements a repair loop with max_retries=2
Feeds validation error messages back to the LLM to request corrected JSON

name: Circuit Breaker Pattern State Lifecycle
query: How does the Circuit Breaker pattern work in distributed microservices to prevent cascading system failures? Detail its three states: Closed, Open, and Half-Open.
retrieval_context: The Circuit Breaker pattern protects distributed microservices by intercepting outbound requests. In the Closed state, requests pass through normally; consecutive failures increment a counter. When the failure threshold is breached, the circuit trips to Open, instantly rejecting requests with fail-fast errors without contacting the failing downstream service. After a configured timeout, the breaker enters Half-Open, allowing a limited probe trial of requests to determine if the downstream service has recovered. If successful, it resets to Closed; if failures persist, it returns to Open.
expected_facts: Closed state: normal operation routing requests to downstream service
Open state: trips after failure threshold, fails fast without downstream calls
Half-Open state: trial period after sleep window allowing limited probe requests
description: Standard software architecture query testing direct synthesis without external network or retriever calls.

name: Merge Sort vs Quick Sort Complexity & Cache Locality
query: Compare the time and space complexity of Merge Sort and Quick Sort in their best, average, and worst cases. Why is Merge Sort preferred for linked lists?
retrieval_context: Merge Sort has guaranteed O(n log n) time complexity in best, average, and worst cases, with O(n) auxiliary space for arrays. Quick Sort has O(n log n) best and average time complexity, but degrades to O(n^2) worst case when pivot selection is poor, with O(log n) stack space. Merge Sort is preferred for linked lists because nodes can be rearranged in-place by altering pointers without extra memory overhead (O(1) auxiliary space), and it operates sequentially without requiring random access indexing.

Quick Sort has O(n log n) average but O(n^2) worst case
